summary: Feed s160_double is degraded: IDS receives 12.6% duplicate packets and 19.4% one-way TCP sessions (26/134), preventing complete bidirectional flow reassembly and reducing detection coverage.

findings.root_cause: 12.6% duplicates (283/2243 packets, threshold 5%) indicates overlapping SPAN sessions or dual TAP feeds aggregated without deduplication on the packet broker, forwarding the same packet twice to the IDS port.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS wastes CPU/capacity on duplicate processing, inflates flow/packet counters, risks false positives and missed true positives due to state confusion and reduced headroom for real traffic.

recommended_fix.why: Broker-level deduplication removes identical packets seen within a short window from overlapping SPAN/TAP sources before delivery, eliminating 12.6% waste without losing unique traffic.

findings.root_cause: 19.4% of TCP sessions are one-way (26/134, threshold 10%) - broker is not aggregating both directions of a flow to this IDS port. Likely separate ingress/egress SPANs or asymmetric routing with per-direction forwarding or incorrect load-balancing hash splitting client->server and server->client across different tool ports.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS requires both directions (needs_both_directions=true) for TCP reassembly and stateful signature detection. One-way visibility blinds stream reassembly, allows evasion, and causes missed exploits, callbacks, and incomplete session logging.

recommended_fix.why: Aggregating both directions of each 5-tuple flow to the same IDS port restores full bidirectional sessions required for stateful IDS detection.
